newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline's early strong gains partly reversed.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline's early strong gains partly reversed.

text.p: European gasoline prices on the barge and swaps markets fell back slightly on Monday after a sharp early rise on strong fundamentals.
The afternoon saw no fresh confirmed barge trades on the Eurograde market after a string of deals in the morning for second half July and first half August.

Traders said availability was restricted by low refinery margins and refiners' preference for maximizing relatively high-priced naphtha at a time when there was a fair degree on physical demand, including current requirements for volumes into Poland and eastern Germany.
Swaps were talked at around $189 for August, still around $2 up on the day, while Eurograde barges were seen in the $190-$192 range for second half July and $190-$191 range for first half August.

Some physical talk was seen, with an ARA trader heard bidding for Med 0.50 gasoline at $197 and a cargo in the north heard offered as high as $200, reflecting the market view that the cargo premium over barges was widening.
